title: Reordered Power of 2
summary: Given an integer n , rearrange its digits into any order, ensuring the resulting number has a non-zero leading digit.
statement: Given an integer n , rearrange its digits into any order, ensuring the resulting number has a non-zero leading digit. Determine if such a rearrangement can produce a number that is a power of two.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 10^9; reordered decimal digits cannot start with zero.
Return whether some permutation forms a power of two.
hints: Digit permutations share exactly the same sorted digit signature.
Compare n’s signature with every power of two in range.
Equal multisets are precisely the condition for a no-leading-zero permutation; powers never begin with zero.
editorial: Equal multisets are precisely the condition for a no-leading-zero permutation; powers never begin with zero.

tests.explanation: Neither 10 nor 01 is a power of two.
